description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) seeks innovative approaches to address challenges related to quantum computing. Proposed research should investigate approaches that enable revolutionary advances in design, engineering, test, and evaluation of such systems. Specifically excluded is research that primarily results in evolutionary improvements to the existing state of practice. To rapidly capitalize on new opportunities, DARPA announces the QBI 2026 opportunity, which seeks specific solutions to targeted challenges related to developing utility-scale quantum computers, as defined in specific QBI topic (QBIT) calls. Each QBIT will (1) outline specific details regarding the research topic of interest and (2) provide proposal and submission instructions, including the due date for proposal submission, in addition to those outlined in this PA. Proposals must only be submitted in response to a QBIT. Proposals submitted directly to this PA will not be considered.

title: High-Capacity Hydrogen and Hydrogen Isotope Getters
description: Even small amounts of hydrogen can damage sensitive equipment over time. As hydrogen accumulates inside sealed environments, it can corrode metals, weaken structural materials, degrade electronic components, and, in some applications, create explosion hazards. Preventing that buildup is essential for maintaining the reliability and safety of many high-value systems. Hydrogen getters are materials built into sealed devices and systems to remove hydrogen before it can accumulate. Like a moisture absorber, they remove an unwanted gas. Instead of trapping water, however, they chemically react with hydrogen and lock it away permanently. Depending on the application, a getter may take the form of a pellet, coating, thin film, powder, or printable material. Many commercially available getters rely on zirconium-based materials that offer limited hydrogen storage capacity, require activation before use, or operate effectively only within a narrow temperature range. Some also depend on costly vacuum-deposition manufacturing processes that limit design flexibility. Los Alamos researchers have developed a new class of hydrogen getters designed to overcome these limitations. The materials capture hydrogen and its isotopes, including deuterium and tritium, across a broad range of operating conditions without requiring activation while offering significantly higher storage capacity and greater flexibility for manufacturing and product integration. Value Proposition Hydrogen can quietly build up inside sealed devices and industrial systems, shortening equipment life and creating safety risks. Los Alamos National Laboratory has developed a new class of high-capacity hydrogen getters that permanently remove hydrogen before it causes damage. Compared with conventional getters, this technology stores more hydrogen, operates across a wider range of conditions, and can be manufactured in multiple forms for easy integration into commercial products. Hydrogen uptake rate decreases as getter materials fill with hydrogen. Compared with a conventional getter (brown), the LANL high-capacity getter (green) maintains rapid hydrogen capture over a much larger storage capacity. Advantages Stores significantly more hydrogen than many conventional getter materials. Permanently removes hydrogen, improving long-term reliability in sealed systems. Operates across a broad temperature range without activation. Captures hydrogen even at pressures well below atmospheric levels. Selectively removes hydrogen in mixed-gas environments. Hydrogen uptake rates can be tailored to specific applications. Compatible with polymers and available as films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, and printable pastes for flexible product integration. Reduces projected material and manufacturing costs compared with many zirconium-based getter technologies. Scalable manufacturing supports applications ranging from miniature electronics to large industrial systems. Technology Description The getter materials chemically react with hydrogen and its isotopes to form stable compounds that permanently lock the hydrogen inside the material, providing long-term protection for sealed devices and industrial equipment. The technology is based on a novel organic alkyne chemistry. Alkynes are carbon-containing molecules that readily react with hydrogen, allowing the material to store substantially more hydrogen than many conventional getter systems. Unlike many commercial getters, these materials operate without activation and continue to perform across a broad temperature range. They also selectively capture hydrogen in the presence of gases such as helium, nitrogen, argon, and methane, making them well suited for complex industrial and vacuum environments. The hydrogen capture rate can be tailored by adjusting the catalyst formulation for specific operating conditions. Hydrogen capture has also been demonstrated at pressures well below atmospheric conditions, expanding the range of potential applications. The materials are compatible with polymers and other common manufacturing materials, allowing them to be incorporated into films, coatings, pellets, powders, strands, adhesives, foams, and printable pastes. title: Greece, Lithuania, Poland, Cyprus – Research and experimental development services – Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP)
description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. title: Cost Effective On-Base Parcel Delivery Solutions (RAFL, RAFM, RAFF, United Kingdom)
description: The 48th Contracting Squadron at Royal Air Force (RAF) Lakenheath, United Kingdom, seeks to identify qualified sources and cost-effective commercially practical solutions capable of providing reliable on-base parcel delivery services for RAF Lakenheath (RAFL), RAF Mildenhall (RAFM), and RAF Feltwell (RAFF) in the United Kingdom. Purpose of Market Research: Our primary objective is to gain an understanding of how the Government's required delivery outcome can be achieved at a reasonable/sustainable cost while also being reliable. The Government is not seeking an unnecessarily complex or premium delivery model where a simpler commercial solution could reliably satisfy the requirement. *This RFI is issued solely for market research and acquisition planning purposes. It does not constitute a solicitation, Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or promise to issue a future solicitation. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. The Government will not reimburse respondents for costs associated with preparation or submission of information in response to this RFI. * Background: Personnel who live or work on RAFL, RAFM, and RAF Feltwell receive both personal and official parcels from commercial delivery companies. The most common carriers, presently, have been DPD, DHL, Evri, FedEx, Parcelforce, UPS, Amazon, and Royal Mail. Royal Mail/Parcelforce are the only delivery entities that presently have installation access and deliver directly to the on-base addresses. Other commercial parcel delivery companies do not have installation access, creating challenges in completing delivery to the intended on-base residence or agency. The Government is exploring a recurring parcel delivery service capable of receiving or otherwise obtaining parcels from commercial carriers that do not have installation access and completing final delivery to the intended residence or agency on RAF Lakenheath, RAF Mildenhall, or RAF Feltwell. The Government seeks industry�s recommendations regarding the most efficient and economical means of accomplishing this outcome. Packages, after they are picked up by a neighbor, have an average dwell time of 2 weeks before the intended recipients of the packages become aware that a neighbor had received their package on their behalf. The Government is particularly interested in solutions that make use of existing commercial capabilities and minimize unnecessary Government-specific processes, facilities, equipment, or infrastructure. Primary Constraints: Installation access and funding will be the primary constraints and will be the biggest factors considered in developing the desired solution. Presently installation access for local nationals can take upwards of 7 months due to the MOD clearance/background check process. The government is not aware of any route to expedite the processing of packages. It has been observed that the delivery driver experiences a high level of turnover, unpredictable routes for drivers, and criminal records that prohibit access to the installation which affects the parcel delivery companies� ability to obtain installation access for their drivers. Drones are not permitted on or near these installations and should not be included in identified solutions. Government-provided escorts will not be available as an interim staffing or access solution. Respondents should consider these conditions when describing their proposed solution and should identify how they could achieve the required staffing and access capability within the anticipated transition period. Respondents should also identify cost-effective approaches for maintaining sufficient access-qualified staffing without unnecessarily increasing the number of personnel requiring installation access. Estimated Parcel Volume: Available information indicates that approximately 1,000 parcels per week are associated with RAF Lakenheath that are being coordinated for pick-up at businesses near the installation. Should a reliable delivery service be established, the volume of parcels is expected to at least triple. Comparable parcel-volume information is not currently available for RAFM or RAFF. The bases in order of highest estimated volume to lowest are as follows: RAFL, RAFF, RAFM. Suggested solutions will need to be scalable to fluctuate as personnel to the bases fluctuate and parcel volume fluctuates. Respondents should identify how uncertainty and fluctuations in parcel volume would affect their recommended solution and pricing. Respondents are also encouraged to suggest a Contract Line Item Number (CLIN) structure best suited to their recommendation. Respondents are specifically encouraged to identify approaches that allow the service to scale efficiently as parcel volume changes without requiring the Government to pay for unnecessary excess capacity during lower-volume periods. Desired Outcome: The desired outcome is a reliable and cost-effective service capable of delivering eligible parcels from commercial delivery companies that do not have installation access to the residence or agency on the installation that ordered the item. The service would be expected to support RAFL, RAFM, and RAFF. All three installations are anticipated to be included from the very beginning of performance. The service would handle both personal and official parcels. Delivery service is expected seven days per week. For residential deliveries, parcels that do not require a recipient signature may be left at the recipient's door (or in a safe place designated by their delivery notes). The Government recognizes that commercial carriers may transfer parcels at different times throughout the day. Respondents should identify any operational assumptions, carrier coordination, cutoff times, or other conditions necessary to accomplish daily delivery. Solutions should not be disruptive, so the preference is to find a solution to deliver packages by 1700 each day ensuring no nighttime disruptions. title: Technology Licensing Opportunity: Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements
description: Note: This is a technology licensing opportunity. No procurement, grants, or funding opportunities are associated with this notice. Room-Temperature Electrochemical Metallization of Rare Earth Elements A low-energy, low-hazard alternative to molten-salt electrolysis for sustainable REE production. Technology Summary This invention introduces a method to produce metallic rare earth elements (REEs) through room-temperature electrometallization in anhydrous electrolytes. By leveraging unique ion-pairing interactions, Lewis acid-base chemistry, and interfacial structuring, the system enables efficient REE reduction and stable metal formation without the extreme energy use or toxic byproducts of conventional fused salt electrolysis. Problem Addressed High cost & regulatory barriers: Current molten-salt electrolysis (600�1200 �C) generates toxic HF gas and rare earth fluoride waste, triggering costly EPA and OSHA compliance requirements. Environmental impact: Legacy processes produce hazardous waste with long-term contamination risks, leading to industry abandonment in North America. Supply chain dependence: Metallic REEs are only produced at scale in China, creating vulnerabilities for U.S. manufacturers and defense applications. Solution The invention replaces high-temperature fused salt electrolysis with an ambient-temperature electrochemical process. The approach integrates three synergistic innovations: Tuned electrolyte nucleophilicity � enabling more efficient reduction pathways. Lewis acid-base coordination control � stabilizing the ligand environment during deposition. Interfacial electrochemical structuring � improving reaction kinetics and metal stability. This combination allows REE electrodeposition at room temperature, reducing both energy demand and hazardous byproduct formation. This invention enables dual functionality, electrodeposition and (in-situ) electrorefining. Key Advantages Lower energy consumption � eliminates the need for 600�1200 �C molten salt processes. Reduced environmental liabilities � avoids HF gas emissions and toxic fluoride salt accumulation. Safer operations � circumvents EPA and RCRA compliance barriers tied to FSE. Domestic supply potential � enables North American REE production for critical industries. Scalable platform � adaptable to multiple REEs including neodymium, samarium, dysprosium, and terbium. Market Applications Permanent magnets � essential for EV traction motors, wind turbines, and energy-efficient refrigeration. Defense systems � critical components for satellites, communication devices, and advanced weapons. Lightweight alloys � enhancing aerospace and automotive materials. Electronics � miniaturized devices requiring REE-based components. Battery technologies � advanced REE-containing chemistries for high-performance storage.

ANTICIPATED ACQUISITION STRATEGY: The acquisition strategy for this requirement will be determined based on the responses to this Sources Sought notice and other market research. The Government is considering several compliant acquisition pathways to ensure the successful delivery of this complex Design-Build project in Peru. All interested firms are strongly encouraged to submit a comprehensive capabilities statement, as the information received will be critical in determining the final method of procurement. The primary anticipated strategy is a Two-Phase Design-Build procurement under the authority of FAR Part 36.3. In this scenario, the Government would issue a public Phase 1 solicitation requesting offeror qualifications. Based on these qualifications, the Government would down-select the most highly qualified firms (typically no more than five) who would then be eligible to compete in Phase 2 and submit detailed technical and price proposals. Under this authority, the Government would create a list of pre-qualified firms that demonstrate the essential standards for technical capability, financial stability, and in-country operational capacity. Future solicitations for this requirement would then be limited to firms on this established QBL. title: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030)
description: Henkilöstön osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut 2027-2029 (2030) Hankinnan kohteena on Jyväskylän kaupungin henkilöstöön kuuluvien esimiesten ja työyhteisöjen osaamisen kehittämisen palvelut. Hankintaa ei ole jaettu osiin, sillä jakaminen ei palvelun luonteen vuoksi ole tarkoituksenmukaista eikä jaosta saada selkeää. Sen sijaan poolista tehdään melko suuri, jotta saadaan laaja-alainen asiantuntijuus turvattua. Palveluiden hankinta voidaan toteuttaa joko henkilöstöhallinnon tai työyksiköiden esimiesten hankkimana tilanteissa, joissa on havaittu kehittämistarvetta. Tuleva hankinta koskee kaikkia Jyväskylän kaupungin toimialoja ja liikelaitoksia. Tarjouskilpailulla muodostetaan 15 yrityksen/toimijan pooli, tai useamman, mikäli mukaan ei saada vähintään 25 valmentajaa. Jos soveltuvia tarjouksia on vähemmän kuin 15, valitaan kaikki soveltuvat tarjoukset. Jotta turvataan pientenkin toimijoiden pääseminen hankintaan mukaan, rinnakkaisia tarjouksia ei hyväksytä, ja yksi yritys/toimija voi tarjota 1-3 asiantuntijaa pooliin. Palvelun käynnistämisen tavoiteaika on 1.3.2027. Lisätiedot hankinnan kohteesta tarjouspyynnöstä ja sen liitteistä.,

title: Vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut
description: Vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut Hankinnan kohteena on vartiointi- ja hälytyskeskuspalvelut Kainuun hyvinvointialueella. Palvelun kohteena ovat Tilaajan Toimeksiantosopimuksissa määrittelemät kohteet. Turvallisuuspalvelut sisältävät paikallisvartiointia, kiertävä vartiointi (ent. piirivartiointi), hälytys- ja tilausvartiointia. Vartiointipalveluiden tarkoituksena on ylläpitää ja edistää turvallisuutta sovituilla vartioimisalueilla ja -kohteissa, sekä tarvittaessa ryhtyä lain (Laki yksityisistä turvallisuuspalveluista 1085/2015) sallimissa rajoissa toimenpiteisiin turvallisuuden palauttamiseksi. Vartiointi - ja hälytyskeskuspalvelu koostuu mm. seuraavista palveluista (tarkemmin kuvattu Palvelukuvauksessa (liite 6): -Paikallisvartiointi; siihen liittyvä tilausvartiointi (yksittäinen tehtävä etukäteen tilattu) -Hälytyskäynnit -Kiertävä vartiointi (ent. piirivartiointi) -Hälytyskeskuspalvelu (esim. murtohälytysjärjestelmien testaus/hälytyksen siirrot, hälytysten vastaanottaminen) -Henkilöturvaan, omaisuuteen ja kiinteistöön liittyvät hälytykset Kainuun hyvinvointialueen toimitiloissa ja kiinteistöissä (mm. ovien kiinniolojen seuranta, jääkaappihälytykset, N-kaappien hälytykset, henkilöstön avustaminen pukukaappien avauksessa) -Yleiset kiinteistön pitoon liittyvät aputyöt (esim. puku- ja laukkukaappien avaukset vikatilanteessa, tarvittaessa pukukaappien tarkastukset), Vuototilanteissa huolto/kalustesulkujen sulkeminen (päivystävä huoltomies ohjeistaa), lipunnosto Kainuun keskussairaalassa -Aula- ja paikallisvartiointipalvelut Kainuun keskussairaalassa: (esim. väliaikaisten kulkuoikeuksien ja - lupien hallinta, palohälytyksiin reagointi ja keskussairaalan kuulutukset) Hälytyskeskuspalvelut sisältyvät toimeksiantosopimukseen ilman erillistä korvausta palvelukuvauksen mukaisesti. Hälytyskeskuspalvelun tarkoituksena on jatkuva päivystäminen (24/7 palvelu), joka mahdollistaa erilaisten palvelupyyntöjen vastaanottamisen ja niihin reagoimisen.,

title: Evaluering- Operativt SaLTo
description: Bydel Alna har behov for ekstern bistand til evaluering av prosjektet Operativt SaLTo. Prosjektet dreier seg om å finne nye metoder for å motvirke og forebygge ungdomskriminalitet. Evalueringen skal gi et faglig og operativt beslutningsgrunnlag for videreutvikling, videreføring og eventuell implementering av prosjektets samarbeidsmodell og arbeidsmetodikk. Oppdraget skal belyse hvordan modellen fungerer i praksis, identifisere hvilke deler som bør videreføres, justeres eller avsluttes, og vurdere organisatoriske forutsetninger for videreføring. Et særskilt formål er å vurdere hvordan erfaringer, metoder og arbeidsformer fra prosjektet kan tas i bruk i ny organisasjon etter bydelsreform fra 2028. Estimert verdi på anskaffelsen er 700 000 kroner ekskl. mva.

title: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) Modeling & Simulation Support
description: This Request for Information (RFI) is being issued by the Department of the Army, on behalf of Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) Fires. PAE Fires is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify qualified, experienced, and interested sources capable of providing specialized engineering, modeling, simulation, and software support for the Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) Project Office in support of the AN/TPY-2 Terminal Mode. The contractor shall provide support for development, integration, and testing of the THAAD Modeling and Simulation (M&S) products. The contractor shall deliver software products for the AN/TPY-2 Terminal Mode, including incremental development releases, Engineering Releases and Final Releases. The contractor shall deliver updated software documentation for AN/TPY-2 Terminal Mode, including appropriately red-lined documents. The contractor shall support integration of software into the THAAD M&S products, to include on-site support as needed. The contractor shall support the resolution of related observations made by the THAAD M&S products during all phases of development and integration, as well as on-going system testing. Note that this is not a request for quotes. A determination by the Government not to compete this requirement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. This RFI seeks industry comments to assist the Government in locating potential sources with the ability to satisfy its requirement. Please provide the following Point of Contact Information: Company: Address: Point of Contact: Phone Number: Fax Numbers: Email Address: DUNS Number: CAGE Code: Business Size and Classification (Large Business, Small Business, 8(a), Woman-Owned/Economically Disadvantaged Woman-Owned, Historically Underutilized Business Zone (HUBZone), Veteran-Owned, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned): Potential sources are invited to submit a Capabilities Statement up to five (5) pages per each of the four (4) major tasks, as described above, to the "RFI: THAAD Modeling and Simulation Support". All responses should be submitted via e-mail address to jonathan.w.dickens.civ@army.mil and sean.c.allan.civ@mail.mil. Only attach MS Word/Excel compatible files or Adobe Acrobat PDF files in electronic correspondence. PM THAAD will not acknowledge receipt of responses to this RFI. description: The Pre-CommerciAl ProCuremenT of Innovative Personal ProtectiVe Equipment for First REsponders (ACTIVE PCP) project addresses critical gaps in personal protective equipment (PPE). It responds to the need to keep first responders safe and operationally effective during evolving threats, from CBRN incidents and HAZMAT situations to terrorism, industrial accidents, natural disasters, and other complex emergencies. ACTIVE PCP involves public safety buyers and end-users in defining unmet needs and guiding industry R&D towards solutions. ACTIVE PCP procures R&D services through Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP). // Tenderers are invited to propose innovative PPE solutions for first responders, police, firefighters, and emergency medical services operating in complex CBRN and HAZMAT environments. Following the phased PCP model, the procurement supports R&D up to the development of a limited volume of first products. It comprises 3 competitive Phases, with fewer Tenderers progressing at each stage so that those offering the strongest response to the PCP's technical challenge are selected. // The PCP will be implemented by means of a Framework Agreement (FA) with call-offs for specific contracts for each of the 3 R&D phases (altogether ‘Contracts’). Greek law governs the Contracts. The GDPR Processing Agreement – if applicable – will be governed by the law of the Member State in which each pilot will take place during Phase 3. The FA will remain binding for the duration of all phases for which Contractors remain in the PCP. There will be no renegotiations. // KEMEA will be the Lead Procurer throughout all the phases of ACTIVE PCP. // Tenderers that are awarded a FA will also be awarded a specific contract for Phase 1 (evaluation of tenders for the FA and Phase 1 are combined). Tenderers are therefore asked not only to submit their detailed offer for Phase 1, but also to state their goals, and to outline their plans (including price conditions) for Phases 2 and 3. // The three Phases are: (i) Phase 1: Solution Design. A FA and a Specific Contract for Phase 1 will be awarded to at least six (6) contractors; (ii) Phase 2: Prototyping. A call-off will be organised for Phase 2, with the aim of awarding at least three (3) Phase 2 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 1 will be eligible for Phase 2. The procurers will validate the Phase 2 prototypes; and (iii) Phase 3: Original development and testing. A second call-off will be organised for Phase 3, with the aim of awarding a minimum of two (2) Phase 3 contracts. Only offers from Contractors that successfully completed Phase 2 will be eligible for Phase 3. The procurers will validate the Phase 3 prototypes. // Offers for the next phase will be requested together with the End of Phase deliverables of the previous phase. I.e., all Contractors of the previous phase have the right to submit offers for the next phase (together with their End of Phase Report). A Contractor must have been awarded a Specific Contract for Phase 1 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 2. Likewise, a Contractor must have been awarded Specific Contracts for Phases 1 and 2 in order to be considered eligible for Phase 3. The maximum total budget for this PCP is 3.650.000 EUR including VAT, taxes and other related fees and costs). // The maximum budget per phase and the maximum budget per Contractor (excluding VAT, including taxes and other related fees and costs) are as follows: For Phase 1 (Solution Design): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €47,043.00; Total subcontracting cost for phase 1: €282,258.05. For Phase 2 (Prototyping): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €483,870.97; Total subcontracting cost for phase 2: €1,451,612.90. For Phase 3 (Original development and testing): Subcontracting cost per contractor: €604,838.71; Total subcontracting cost for phase 3: €1,209,677.42. For Phase 1, contracts will be financed until the remaining budget is insufficient to fund the next best tender. Dort sind laut Studie acht zusätzliche Klassenzimmer und ein Nebenraum mit zusammen rund 570 m² Nutzfläche vorgesehen. Die Planung berücksichtigt zudem die Sicherstellung der natürlichen Belichtung der Aula, die Nutzung der neuen Dachflächen für Photovoltaik sowie die weitere Ausarbeitung des Brandschutzkonzepts. • Zu vergebende Leistungen: Stufenweise Beauftragung der Leistungsphasen 2 anteilig und 3 - 9; Objektplanung gem. §34 HOAI 2021
